newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Swiss/EU no nearer bilateral transport deal.
newsitem.headline: Swiss/EU no nearer bilateral transport deal.

text.p: Switzerland and the European Union appeared no nearer a deal on Tuesday on bilateral road and air links, with the European Commission issuing a terse statement on the latest talks three hours before they ended.
"Discussion focused on the aspect of the negotiations relating to land transport and both sides were able to agree the broad structure of a possible agreement...," the Commission statement said.

Swiss Federal Transport Minister Moritz Leuenberger confirmed that position to reporters after talks ended, saying both sides had agreed the approach which he hoped would bear fruit before the summer holidays.

"The climate was very positive, we found a concept but still have no deal on the figures," the Swiss minister said in reference to his country's plans for a road user charge for heavy trucks in place of the existing transit ban.

Negotiators are looking for an overall deal including agreement on common truck weight limits, rail freight transit infrastructure and service guarantees, a two-way safeguard clause, improved market access for hauliers and truck transit quotas from the outset.
The meeting was scheduled to include Leuenberger along with Dutch Transport Minister and current EU president Annemarie Jorritsma and, European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock.
Main differences concern how much trucks should pay to transit Switzerland and the EU's demand for immediate access for its 40-tonne trucks to Swiss industrial and commercial centres.

Kinnock has previously rejected a Swiss offer to replace the present ban on trucks weighing more than 28-tonnes with universal road charges, saying the price offered by Berne would perpetuate the diversion of traffic through Austria and France.
